### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A14 and A15 were never observed (0 of 200 traces). In the later window, A14 appears in about 44 in 100 traces and A15 in about 56 in 100, in each case exactly once per trace containing it [OCC001, OCC002].
- In the earlier window, A35 was always followed directly by A20: all of its observed outgoing transitions went to A20, and the pair was consecutive (lag 1) in essentially every trace. In the later window, A35's outgoing transitions go to A15 in about 56 in 100 cases and to A14 in about 44 in 100, with a direct A35→A20 transition remaining in only about 1 in 200 [DIR003, LAG001].
- In the later window, A14 and A15 each lead to A20 in 100 in 100 of their observed outgoing transitions; neither activity was observed before, so no earlier outgoing profile exists [DIR001, DIR002].
- A14 and A15 act as mutually exclusive alternatives: in the later window they never occur in the same trace — about 44 in 100 traces contain only A14, about 56 in 100 only A15, and about 1 in 200 contain neither — whereas in the earlier window neither appeared at all [REL001].
- Ordering in the later window: whenever A14 occurs, A35 comes before it and A14 before A20 (about 44 in 100 traces); the same holds for A15 (about 56 in 100 traces) [REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005].
- Consequently, the distance between A35 and A20 shifted from immediate succession (lag 1 in all earlier traces) to one intervening event (lag 2 in about 995 in 1000 later traces) [LAG001].
- When they occur, A14 and A15 sit at about 36% of the trace's event positions on average (median about 0.35); this is event position, not clock time [POS001, POS002].
- All flagged items show differences larger than in about 995 of 1000 random re-splits of the pooled data, and the number of items (13) is far above the roughly 0.33 expected by chance in an unchanged process across the 67 tested units [OCC001, OCC002, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, POS001, POS002, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, LAG001].

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that, in the later window, a new step was inserted between A35 and A20: A35, which previously led directly to A20, now leads to either A14 or A15 — two mutually exclusive alternatives taken in roughly a 44-to-56 split — and the chosen activity then leads on to A20, so A20 is reached one step later than before. This rests on direct relational and successor evidence: the redirection of A35's outgoing transitions, the new A14→A20 and A15→A20 transitions, the consistent A35-before-A14/A15-before-A20 ordering, and the lag between A35 and A20 changing from 1 to 2 [DIR003, DIR001, DIR002, REL001, LAG001].

The picture is internally consistent: the roughly 1 in 200 later traces in which A35 still leads directly to A20 match the share of traces containing neither A14 nor A15, suggesting the old direct path persists rarely. The items largely describe one coherent structural difference rather than independent phenomena, so they should not be read as multiple confirmations. Limitations: the evidence cannot show what governs the choice between A14 and A15, and zero participation in the earlier window strictly means only that A14 and A15 were not exercised in those 200 traces, not that they were absent from the underlying process — although a behaviour occurring in roughly half of later traces is unlikely to be missed by chance in a stable process [DIR003, LAG001, REL001, OCC001, OCC002].

Now let's understand the behaviour.

OCC001: A14 — before: 0 occurrences per trace, 0% participation. After: 0.44 mean occurrences per trace, 44% participation (88 of 200 traces). So A14 was absent before, appears in about 44 in 100 traces after, exactly once each (recurrence support 0, mean = participation, so one occurrence per containing trace).

OCC002: A15 — before: 0. After: 0.555 mean occurrences, 55.5% participation (111 of 200 traces). Again one occurrence per containing trace.

DIR001: outgoing transitions of A14 — before: empty (A14 never observed). After: 100% of outgoing transitions go to A20. So after, A14 is always followed by A20.

DIR002: A15 — before empty; after: 100% to A20. A15 always followed by A20.

DIR003: A35 — before: 100% of outgoing transitions to A20. After: 55.5% to A15, 44% to A14, 0.5% to A20. Support before 200, after 200. So A35 previously always led to A20; now it leads to A15 in about 56 in 100 cases and A14 in about 44 in 100 cases, with A20 almost never directly.

POS001: A14 position — after: mean position ~0.36 of trace (normalized position presumably), support 0.44. Before: no support. So A14 occurs at about 36% through the trace.

POS002: A15 — after mean position ~0.365, support 0.555.

REL001: A14 & A15 — before: neither in 100% of traces. After: A_only (A14 without A15) 44%, B_only (A15 without A14) 55.5%, neither 0.5%, cooccurrence 0. So A14 and A15 never occur in the same trace; they are alternatives. In the after window, every trace contains exactly one of them (99.5% — 0.44 + 0.555 + 0.005 = 1.0). So one of A14/A15 executes in essentially every trace, but never both.

REL002: A14 & A20 — before: B_only (A20 without A14) 100%. After: cooccurrence 44%, A_before_B (A14 before A20) 44%, B_only 56%. So in the after window, whenever A14 occurs, A20 also occurs and A14 comes first.

REL003: A14 & A35 — before: B_only (A35 without A14) 100%. After: cooccurrence 44%, B_before_A (A35 before A14) 44%. So A35 comes before A14 whenever A14 occurs.

REL004: A15 & A20 — before: B_only 100%. After: cooccurrence 55.5%, A_before_B (A15 before A20) 55.5%.

REL005: A15 & A35 — before: B_only 100%. After: cooccurrence 55.5%, B_before_A (A35 before A15) 55.5%.

LAG001: A35 → A20 lag — before: lag 1 (immediately consecutive) in 100% of traces. After: lag 2 in 99.5%. So A35 and A20 were directly consecutive before; after, there is one event between them.

Putting it together:

Before: A35 is always immediately followed by A20 (lag 1, DIR003 100% A20, LAG001 lag 1). A14 and A15 never occur.

After: A35 is followed by A15 in ~56% of cases and A14 in ~44% (DIR003). A14 and A15 are mutually exclusive alternatives (REL001). Whichever occurs is followed by A20 (DIR001, DIR002), and A20 now comes one step later after A35 (LAG001 lag 2) because the new activity (A14 or A15) is inserted between A35 and A20. REL002/REL003: A35 before A14 before A20. REL004/REL005: A35 before A15 before A20.

So the hypothesis: an activity (A14 or A15, chosen as alternatives — roughly 44/56 split) was inserted between A35 and A20. Before, A35 → A20 directly; after, A35 → (A14 | A15) → A20.

This is a structural change: insertion of new activities. The evidence is direct: OCC shows A14/A15 absent then present; DIR shows A35's outgoing transitions changed from A20 to A14/A15, and A14/A15's outgoing to A20; REL shows ordering A35 < A14/A15 < A20; LAG shows the A35→A20 distance changed from 1 to 2.

Screening: 13 items vs 0.33 expected — many times larger. So chance cannot explain the count.

Support level: Supported hypothesis. The evidence directly shows the insertion: new activities appear, the edge A35→A20 is replaced by A35→A14/A15→A20, ordering relations confirm, and the lag change confirms. Consistent across OCC, DIR, POS, REL, LAG. All items have empirical_strength ~0.995.

One limitation: we cannot tell from positional data whether clock-time changed; but that's not relevant. Another competing explanation: the process might have had these activities in traces outside the before window sample — but with 200 traces and zero occurrences, that's unlikely; still, finite sample caveat. Also, we can't determine why the choice between A14 and A15 is made (44/56 split) — is that a routing share change? Actually the choice between A14 and A15 is new behaviour; the split ~44/56 is observed but the driver is unknown. Also note: is this "existing paths taken with different frequencies"? No — it's an insertion of new activities, which is a structural change. The condition about path frequency shifts doesn't apply; this is addition of activities.

Also note the small residual: 0.5% of after traces still have A35→A20 directly (DIR003 A20 0.005, LAG001 lag 1 0.005). So in about 1 in 200 traces the old direct path remains.
